title: Dispatch CUS 6: Registrars Propose a Boundary Neither Map Contains
summary: A joint record could recognize both cities without forcing one onto the other.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: Miss Morrow and Miss Hume presented their councils with a paired census entry yesterday. Each volume would keep its own residents at their own addresses. A new column would record the corresponding plot in the other Alderwick as “outside this city’s jurisdiction,” rather than vacant, unlawful, or scheduled for demolition.

The proposal has a practical test. In the two rooms shored after Elsie Hume’s fall, temporary notes of this kind eased the pressure between floor and ceiling. Dr. Saye says the wording matters because an empty plot invites another house to occupy it, while an unlawful one invites officials to remove it. The paired entry grants neither action.

Alderman Dorne supports the trial but asks what becomes of the doorways. Dr. Saye expects them to close if the census volumes no longer describe one city as occupying the other’s land. She has warned households to move any shared belongings back to the side where they belong.

Miss Hume’s council is divided. Several members object to recognizing streets they cannot visit except through openings in their neighbors’ homes. Miss Hume brought Elsie to the hearing with her wrist in a sling. “You can reach my niece by walking through a door,” she told them. “We have done enough measuring to admit she is there.”
The councils will vote separately tomorrow. The notices to vacate remain suspended on both sides, but their stated deadline of 20 February has not been formally withdrawn.
